what_this_is: Raw MCP exchange with the ticket-history server over stdio, captured by backend/scripts/week9_capture_wire.py with no SDK on the client side. 'message' is exactly what was sent (the byte-exact line is in evidence/wire.raw.json). 'annotations' explains every top-level field.
where_the_model_call_happens: The model call happens only in the host - backend/app/agents/week9/agent.py sending chat.completions to Groq - and never in this exchange: not in the MCP client, not in the ticket-history server, which only reads tickets.json.

annotations.jsonrpc: Protocol tag. Always the string "2.0": says this line is a JSON-RPC 2.0 message. MCP does not define its own envelope; it reuses JSON-RPC.
annotations.id: 1 - chosen by the client. The server must echo the same id on its reply so the client can pair request and response. Having an id makes this a request (expects an answer).
annotations.method: "initialize" - the first message of every MCP session. Nothing else may be sent until it completes.
annotations.params: What the client brings to the handshake: protocolVersion (the newest MCP spec revision the client speaks, 2025-11-25), capabilities (features the CLIENT offers the server, e.g. sampling or roots - empty here, we offer none), clientInfo (name/version, for the server's logs only).

annotations.jsonrpc: Protocol tag. Always the string "2.0": says this line is a JSON-RPC 2.0 message. MCP does not define its own envelope; it reuses JSON-RPC.
annotations.id: 1 - the echo of the request id; this is the answer to step 1.
annotations.result: Success payload (a response has either result or error, never both). protocolVersion: the revision the server agrees to speak (it can answer with an older one; the client must then speak that or disconnect). capabilities: what the SERVER offers - tools, resources, prompts; listChanged:false means it will not notify if its tool list changes. serverInfo: name/version - 'support-ops-ticket-history', so we can tell which server answered.

annotations.jsonrpc: Protocol tag. Always the string "2.0": says this line is a JSON-RPC 2.0 message. MCP does not define its own envelope; it reuses JSON-RPC.
annotations.method: "notifications/initialized" - the client confirms the handshake is done; normal traffic may start.
annotations.(no id): There is NO id field: that is what makes this a notification. The server must not reply, and it gets no reply.

annotations.jsonrpc: Protocol tag. Always the string "2.0": says this line is a JSON-RPC 2.0 message. MCP does not define its own envelope; it reuses JSON-RPC.
annotations.method: "tools/list" - discovery: ask the server what tools it offers. This is the call the agent makes at startup instead of having a hard-coded tool list.
annotations.(no params): params omitted: no cursor, so this asks for the first (and here only) page.

tools.name: lookup_ticket
tools.description:
Look up a support ticket by its id (format TCK-nnnn).

    Returns the ticket status, contact count, the customer's tier, the order
    (plan, amount paid, payment status) and the installation / activation status.
    Use it whenever a ticket id is mentioned, before saying anything about that
    customer's order, payment or installation.

tools.name: get_escalation_history
tools.description:
The escalation history behind a ticket (format TCK-nnnn), oldest first:
    when it was escalated, to which team and level, why, and what happened.

    Use it to see whether a customer was promised a callback or a refund and
    whether that promise was kept. An empty list means it was never escalated.

annotations.jsonrpc: Protocol tag. Always the string "2.0": says this line is a JSON-RPC 2.0 message. MCP does not define its own envelope; it reuses JSON-RPC.
annotations.result: result.tools: one entry per tool. name: what the model will call it. description: the docstring - this text IS the prompt the model reads to decide when and how to use the tool. inputSchema: JSON Schema of the arguments (generated from the Python type hints); the agent passes it to Groq unchanged as the function's parameters. No nextCursor, so there are no more pages. These two names are where 'tools before -> after' is counted from.

annotations.jsonrpc: Protocol tag. Always the string "2.0": says this line is a JSON-RPC 2.0 message. MCP does not define its own envelope; it reuses JSON-RPC.
annotations.method: "tools/call" - run one tool. In the agent this is sent only after the MODEL chose the tool and wrote the arguments; the MCP client just forwards that choice.
annotations.params: name: which tool (lookup_ticket). arguments: an object that must match the tool's inputSchema - here {ticket_id: TCK-4471}.

annotations.jsonrpc: Protocol tag. Always the string "2.0": says this line is a JSON-RPC 2.0 message. MCP does not define its own envelope; it reuses JSON-RPC.
annotations.result: content: a list of content blocks the host gives back to the model - one text block holding the ticket as JSON. isError: false means the tool ran fine. A tool failure (bad ticket id) would still be a normal result with isError:true and a readable message, so the model can recover; a JSON-RPC 'error' member instead of 'result' would mean a protocol-level failure (unknown method, malformed request).
